messages:
alex: hitting a weird SSE parse edge in the Node sample app — if the client aborts while the server is mid-chunk, sometimes the client ends up with a trailing partial event and the parser throws. repro steps in the sample app attached

maria: can you paste the partial payload? i want to try with python sdk to see if behaviour matches

alex: paste: ```
event: message
data: {"choices": [{"delta": "hello"}]

``` — note the missing final newline; node sdk treats the final incomplete delimiter as malformed and throws, client disconnect leaves stream in a weird state

taylor: this smells like inconsistent handling of final delimiter vs last-event-id across SDKs. node's streaming parser expects CRLFCRLF really, python SDK tolerates lone LF. we should unify

jamie: fwiw the runtime sometimes flushes partial fragments if connection drops. we added an optimization to emit what we have to avoid token loss. that might be colliding with parsers that require strict framing

alex: so two questions: 1) should sample apps buffer until they see the full event terminator? 2) should SDKs be defensive and accept LF-only final termination?

maria: for parity i think SDKs should be tolerant (best-effort) but sample apps/docs should recommend the strict terminator. also need to check retry behavior: node currently retries on EOF and replays last-event-id, but if the previous stream left a partial last-event-id header we can duplicate chunks

taylor: +1. propose quick fix: node sdk: accept single LF as terminator, but log a debug warning in dev mode. longer term: add a small stateful parser that tolerates truncated tail across reconnects (use last-event-id).

jamie: created a quick repro script (server) — attaching gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/sse-truncation-repro — server intentionally drops after N bytes to simulate client abort. use curl -N to replicate

alex: tried the gist, python SDK reopened with no parse error, node threw `Error: unexpected end of input while parsing event` in the sample app. i can put a minimal fix in the node sample to buffer until `

` arrives and drop partials on disconnect instead of throwing

maria: is this a docs/regression or an SDK bug? sounds like a parity bug to me. we should file an issue and roll a patch to the node sdk sample and maybe the runtime behavior note in docs

jamie: i've opened INF-3197 with logs and the gist. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility

deploy-bot: deployment: node-sdk@canary published (build 548) — contains improved SSE tolerance in dev builds

alex: thanks — i'll validate canary against the sample app and update the sample PR with a small buffering change. if canary looks good, we should backport to stable and update the onboarding quickstart note about streaming framing

maria: also add a tiny test in cross-sdk sample harness that deliberately truncates last chunk and asserts no uncaught parse error. that'll prevent regressions

alex: agreed. i'll add the test in the sample harness repo and link the PR to INF-3197

taylor: once patched, we should mention this in the streaming troubleshooting doc: key bullet points: expected terminator, client abort behavior, last-event-id replay caveats, and recommended sample-app pattern (buffer-on-fragment, idempotent replay)

jamie: +1. moving to triage. thanks everyone for quick loop up
